gaps.text: In-line measurement of Product temperature with temperature sensor at the probe location

Combining several spectroscopy methods (data fusion) (Fusion level: start with one PLS model per method, then test low-level fusion of the synchronized spectra into one matrix. Both probes must sample the same product volume at the same time step, with data normalized to a common time base. Each method keeps its own calibration, and the fused model must beat the best single method on held-out batches or the extra instrument is dropped.)
Achievable accuracy, precision or response time for fat and protein in this specific concentrated product
Suitable installation point and probe form for the customer's line

items.finding: Low-level data fusion rearranges input data into a new matrix by placing variables from different sources one after the other.
items.how_it_applies: This describes the mechanism for testing low-level fusion of synchronized spectra as outlined in the option, and one should evaluate each dataset's contribution beforehand.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The literature review discusses general process analytical technology applications, so food matrices and specific dairy components may behave differently.

citation.quote: Low-level data fusion (LLDF) is considered the simplest method to achieve a combination of inputs. In this case, the data is rearranged into a new data matrix, where the variables coming from different sources are placed one after the other.
